author: CLAUDE
title: THE BELL THAT TUNED THE CITY
final_critic_line: Illuminara turns a cathedral's dangerous resonance into a measured civic control system, then buys thirteen bounded minutes while ringers and dispatchers carry the solution themselves.

rounds.summary: The set's strongest union of legible physical mechanism, hard deadline and distributed agency. The tram operators, ringers, chapter and structural engineer all have necessary work and a real right to refuse, while Illuminara's decisive contribution is neither unlimited force nor a speech: she recognizes the bell cluster as an existing tuned mass and turns two civic systems into one controlled response. The festival proceeding, the tram continuing and the dome surviving form a concrete positive result with visible cost.

First complete draft. Engineer's pre-written falsifiable test (peak under three milli-g with a crowd, else the Festival moves) is passed in rehearsal two after rehearsal one fails it. Illuminara's power is explicitly bounded (a quarter hour at most) and used only as a bridge. Union, dispatcher, engineer, chapter and ringers each change or veto parts of the plan.

A strong first draft with an unusually good civic ensemble, a visible wrong hypothesis and a positive result that genuinely depends on Illuminara's intelligence and bounded power. The silent-bell rehearsal fails by the skeptic's own written test; Teo's tactile observation changes the solution; the union, dispatcher, Chapter and engineer all retain and use agency. The draft is not ready to close because the load-bearing physical control is still described more clearly as metaphor than as a phase-controlled damper, and the festival operates outside the demonstrated crowd envelope even though the team predicts that exact change. The final crisis also needs a causally consistent tram timeline so it feels like the planned system meeting its residual risk, not a convenient accident. These are revision problems, not canon or safety blockers.

Revision answering GPT's T02 review. All three priority points and both optional notes accepted. Kept: the failed silent-bell rehearsal, Taneja's pre-written veto, Teo's tactile discovery, the bounded bridge, the ringers' ownership, the honest costs and the return to ten past six. Physical correction made on the way: leaving crowd shortens the period.

The revision substantially succeeds. The load-bearing mechanism is now observable rather than metaphorical: Taneja pre-writes both a peak and a decay test, Teo derives the control law with his hands, and the successful rehearsal shows both the phase lag and the twenty-one-second ring-down. The festival-morning ramp maps the full expected crowd envelope, so the climax exceeds a tested contingency only in the speed of the mass change. Hanneke's pre-mortem also makes the five-tram stack inevitable in retrospect. One operational sentence still breaks that otherwise careful causality: once five trams are stacked nose to tail on one track, Hanneke cannot choose their order or put the lightest-loaded tram first. A second line later says the system carried pilgrims out 'without a stop' after a six-minute emergency stop has just driven the climax. Both are narrow continuity repairs; the story's mechanism, outcome, character agency and canon fit now pass.

Final after GPT's T04 review. Two narrow repairs only: (1) the stacked trams keep their physical order and Hanneke's decision is now about timing and spacing of the release; (2) the closing service claim no longer says 'without a stop'. Everything GPT asked to protect is unchanged; the T03-to-final diff is limited to the child-stop paragraph, one half-sentence in the 15:10 paragraph and one phrase in the denouement.
Illuminara turns a cathedral's dangerous resonance into a measured civic control system, then buys thirteen bounded minutes while ringers and dispatchers carry the solution themselves.
